▲Foguo Chan Master Kegin of Zhaojue Monastery in Chengdu Prefecture was a successor of the Fifth Patriarch. He was the son of the Luo family of Pengzhou; his ancestors had followed the Confucian tradition for generations.
When the Master was a child, he could memorize a thousand words a day. Once, while wandering through Miaoji Temple, he saw Buddhist scriptures.

Upon reading them three times, he felt a sense of profound longing, as if he had recovered something long lost, and said, "I am surely a śramaṇa from a past life. He then left his home and relied upon [his teacher].
He shaved his head and followed Wenzhao to study the commentaries and expositions. He also received the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* from Minxing. Suddenly he fell ill and was on the verge of death.

He sighed, saying, "The true path to the Nirvāṇa of all Buddhas does not lie within words and phrases. Since I wished to seek it through sound and perceive it through form, it is only natural that I should die.
Thereupon, he abandoned [his studies] and went to the seat of Chan Master Zhengjue Sheng. At that time, Sheng was just...
He struck his back, causing it to bleed, and pointed to it, saying, "This is a single drop from Caoqi. The Master was startled; after a long while, he said, "Is the Way truly like this?
He then immediately set out on foot from Shu, first visiting Yuquan Hao, and subsequently relying upon Jinluan Xin, Dayang Zhe, Huanglong Xin, and Donglin Du.
All of them designated him as a vessel of the Dharma, yet Huitang remarked of him, "In the future..."
The Linji lineage was passed on to him. Finally, he went to see Wuzu, who exhausted his skillful means, yet Wuzu would not grant him approval.
He then remarked that Wuzu was merely trying to shift and manipulate people, speaking insolent words and departing in a fit of indignation. Wuzu said, "Wait until you are struck by a severe fever;
only then will you think of me. When the Master arrived at Jingshan, he contracted a case of smallpox and was utterly exhausted.
He tested this against his usual way of viewing things, but found no efficacy. Tracing back the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself:

"When my illness subsides slightly, I shall return to the Fifth Patriarch. Once his illness was cured, he returned immediately. Upon seeing him, the Patriarch was pleased and ordered him to enter the hall at once;

he then entered the quarters of the attendants (*śayanāsana*). Only half a month had passed when a provincial commissioner, having resigned his office, was returning to Shu and went to visit the Patriarch.
The Provincial Judicial Commissioner asked about this. The Master said, "When you were young, Provincial Commissioner, did you ever read light erotic poetry?

There are two lines that are quite similar: 'Frequently calling for Little Jade, though there is no business at all; it is simply that one wishes for the husband to recognize the voice. The Provincial Commissioner responded, "Yes, yes. The Master said, "But be careful.
Later, when the Master returned and the Commissioner was standing in attendance, he asked, "I heard the Master recite a line from a light erotic poem. The Provincial..."
Xing asked, "Is it so? Guishan said, "He only recognizes sound. The Master said, "I only want the patron to recognize the sound.
Since he has recognized the sound, why is it not so? Guishan asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?"
"The cypress tree in the courtyard, eh? Upon hearing this, the Master suddenly attained realization. He hurriedly went out and saw a chicken fly onto the balustrade and crow with its wings outspread.
He said to himself, "Is this not sound? He then tucked incense in his sleeve, entered the room, and presented what he had realized, offering this verse:
"The golden duck has burned away the fragrance; within the brocade curtains, one is drunk and supported home amidst the sounds of pipes and song. A youth’s..."

"A matter of refined elegance is permitted to be known only by the noble person alone. The Master said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that those of inferior capacity can attain.
I share in your joy. The Master then addressed the elders of the mountain community, saying, "My attendant has attained Zen.
From this point on, wherever he went, he was universally esteemed as a preeminent leader.
Shilong was informed of the treasury [of the teachings] by the late Fifth Patriarch. Throughout his life, the Master was solitary and austere, rarely granting approval to others.
He stood firm and upright like dry wood, relying solely on this one point. He often said of himself, "It is like leaning against Mount Sumeru;
how could I fall into emptiness, playing with slick words to deceive people? Taking that flavorless iron sour-cake, he would thrust it directly at the face of his students.

Have them chew it thoroughly; one must wait until their "bottom falls out" like a bucket, until they have lost all such evil knowledge and views, and not a single thread remains hanging in their breast.
Only when they have penetrated it completely and utterly can you begin to forge them, and only then can you restrain their fists and kicks.
Thereafter, show them the Vajra King’s Precious Sword, to see if they are truly able to practice it and bear its burden, until they are pure and free of even a single [defilement].
As for this matter: mountains are mountains; waters are waters. Yet one must further turn toward that side where the thousand sages have laid their snares and refuse to dwell.
Only then does one accord with the treasury of the true Dharma-eye transmitted from our ancestors down to the present.

When it comes to its practical application for the sake of sentient beings, one must still drive the plowman’s ox and snatch away the hungry man’s food. If one attains verification such that there is tenfold perfection without leakage, this is the very source.
This is the flow of the household way. In the kingdom of Magadha, this command was personally enacted; at Shaolin, facing the wall, the true lineage was fully upheld.
Yet, people of the time misunderstood, eventually valuing silence and stillness as being "without seams or cracks" and "beyond grasp," as if standing like a ten-thousand-fathom cliff.

Little do they realize that this is merely their own fundamental matter; instead, they indulge in the calculations of their own consciousness and opinions, taking this to be a lofty insight. This is a great sickness.
Indeed, the matter from of old was fundamentally not like this. Yantou said: "It is merely a tiny bit revealed right before one's eyes, like the spark struck from stone or a flash of lightning.
If you cannot grasp it, do not harbor doubts; this is the place where those of the highest path tread.
Unless one knows that there is [this], no one can know it. This is like Zhaozhou’s "Go drink tea" and Bimoyan’s raising of the staff.

Xuefeng rolling the ball, Heyang beating the drum, Jueyi’s single finger, Guizong dragging the stone, Xuansha’s “not yet thorough,” Deshan’s staff, and Linji’s shout—all these are top-to-bottom penetrations, directly cutting through the tangles of conceptual entanglement.

These great capacities and great functions, though appearing in a thousand variations and ten thousand differences, all return to a single source; they can untie the adhesions and remove the bonds for others. If one follows [them]...
To provide an explanation: one must immediately grant the fodder of the fundamental portion. It is like ten *shu* of donkey’s milk;

if even a single drop of lion’s milk is added, it all scatters and disperses. If you wish to maintain the transmission from generation to generation in an enduring succession, you must absolutely not accommodate human sentiment and must not allow it to be treated lightly;
only then is it authentic. The final phrase is where one finally reaches the secure barrier. How true!
These words—transcending birth and death and upholding the true mandate—are entirely a matter of this very moment.
Only those who have stepped upon the pivotal bolt at the summit will fully comprehend them.
To the Record Secretary Gao: The orthodox lineage of Linji, from Master Ma and Huangbo onward, has expounded the great function and great capacity.

Shedding the cage and emerging from the nest, they gallop like tigers and race like dragons; swift as shooting stars and flashing like lightning, their rolling up and unfolding, their seizing and releasing, all rely upon their fundamental allotment.
It was continuous and unceasing. Upon reaching Fengxue of Xinghua, his song became even loftier and his faculty even more precipitous.

Like a lion playing in the West River, he brandished the frost-like brilliance of the Vajra King; none who had not deeply penetrated the inner sanctum and personally received his seal of transmission could possibly fathom its origins.

To merely boast of one's own loftiness serves only to increase frivolous discourse (*prapañca*). For the most part, those who possess a majestic and transcendent spirit hold fast beyond conventional boundaries;

they "bend the enemy's weapons without fighting" and "kill without batting an eye. Yet, even this does not yet approximate their true orientation, let alone such acts as shifting the stars and changing the constellations, turning the celestial wheel, and reversing the axis of the earth.

Therefore, [the masters] have demonstrated the Three Mysteries (*san xuan*), the Three Essentials (*san yao*), the Four Critical Examinations (*si liao jian*), and the Four Guests and Hosts (*si bin*).

The Lord Vajrarāja holds a precious sword. The lion crouching on the ground lets out a single roar; it does not function merely as a single roar. It is like a probing pole or a blade of grass in the water.
With one roar, guest and host are distinguished; illumination and function proceed simultaneously. How many have been entangled in such complications!
How many scholars have weighed and measured it with their commentaries! Little do they realize that within the armory of our King there is no such sword. Bring it forth and show it to us!
To merely blink an eye requires one to be among the superior stream; it demands realization, verification, and recognition, pressing directly upon the core while lifting from the periphery.

One must return to the grasses of one’s own original allotment—how could this ever rely on ladders or intermediaries? Consider, for instance, when Baoshou opened the hall and Sansheng pushed forward a monk;
Baoshou struck him immediately. Sansheng said, "If you act as a teacher in this manner, you will not only blind the eyes of this monk, but you will blind all of Zhenzhou."
The people of the city were watching with their own eyes. Shoushan threw down his staff and returned directly to his quarters.
When Xinghua saw that a fellow practitioner had arrived, he shouted. The monk also shouted. Xinghua shouted again. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua said, "Look at this blind fellow!
As the monk hesitated, Xinghua struck him out of the Dharma hall. An attendant asked, "What did you do to provoke him? Xinghua replied, "It was he himself."
There is the expedient and there is the reality. I held my hand before him and crossed it twice, yet he did not understand.
For a blind fellow like this, if I do not strike him, when shall I wait? Behold his authentic ancestral style; it is utterly transcendent and peerless.
It does not value clever maneuvers, but only reveres his eye. To truly uphold the orthodox lineage and maintain the eye of the school, one must penetrate to the very summit.
To the very bottom. To the very bone and marrow. Without the slightest trace of attachment. Utterly and uniquely liberated.
Only then can one receive the authentic transmission and raise this great Dharma banner. Indeed, this great Dharma torch continues the lineage of Mazu, Baizhang, Shoushan, and Yangqi;
it is not a matter of mere usurpation.
Jiù said: "Miaoxi was the foremost disciple who attained the Master’s intent. This record is included here to show the succession of the source and stream;
it cannot be fully chronicled, so this chapter is preserved to convey the essential meaning. Now, as for those who dismiss the fundamental principle:
if this is so even regarding worldly arts and crafts, how much more so regarding the unsurpassed path of enlightenment? If those who now repudiate the school's tenets have not yet crossed over..."

Yet they burn their boats. Those who are mired in names and forms are like those who forget the crossing while clinging to the raft; both are afflicted by illness. Only this chapter is sufficient to rouse them from this state.
I, the old monk Ju-tan Ji, consider Miaoxi to have been the foremost disciple who truly grasped the intent of Foguo.
I have recorded this here to show the succession of the lineage, though I cannot record everything. I preserve this chapter to convey my meaning. And so it ends.
In the general discussion of the Buddha-fruit, regarding the lineages of recent times, there is the case of Yan transmitting it to Shi, and Shi to Gao;
yet they did not reach my Huqiu. Reading this, one cannot help but feel one's hair stand on end.
Han Yue recklessly claimed that Fenggong was his teacher for attaining the mind and Juefan was his teacher for the Dharma seal, whereas the true teacher was Linji. This is correct.
If there were no father in this world, one might claim three different clans as fathers; such a stench would linger for ten thousand years, and their slander would never cease.

Now, since it is said that the current lineage receives its source from the past, how can one disregard that source and instead reach back to claim affiliation with Wuxi (Miaoxi), intermingling them within the tradition?
This is yet another "mixed breed" of Tanji. Formerly, when Foguo was about to...
When returning to Shu, Ying’an Hua wished to accompany him into Shu. [Foguo] personally instructed him to visit Zhangjiao, as Tanji had mentioned.
Why did Foguo deceive Ying’an and not point him toward Miaoxi?
Furthermore, while at Weishou, Miaoxi personally wrote a verse to send to Ying’an, saying: "Severing the path at the First Peak of the Golden Wheel."
A thousand demons and a hundred monsters have all hidden their traces. In recent years, there has been a true report:
it is said that the authentic lineage of Yangqi has been restored. Who is this person?
If I, Hong of Huqiu, were not the heart-disciple of Foguo, then Foguo would not have instructed Ying’an to go see him, nor would Huqiu have emerged from under Ying’an’s guidance. Even Miaoxi...
One should not claim that Yangqi represents the orthodox lineage. At that time, nor should everyone equally refer to Dahui and Ying’an as the two gates of ambrosia.
It is evident that Tanji is of perverse stock and ignorant; he is a most fickle and worldly shaven-headed fellow.
Thus, he uses the technical skills learned from others to metaphorize the fundamental nature of every person.

Having fully attained the path of unsurpassed enlightenment, you have become mired in names and forms, forgetting that you have crossed over and clinging to the raft. Is this not precisely what was spoken from his own lips?
He said that upon reaching the ultimate, one penetrates the Dharma and forgets the Dharma. Yet you fail to reflect that the ancients said:

"When the time arrives, it is like suddenly awakening from a dream, or suddenly remembering what was forgotten. Furthermore, they said: "Whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, one is always within it. This is truly a cause for fear.
To forget for a moment is already insufficient. Now, Tanji’s karmic consciousness is vast and boundless, with no fundamental basis to rely upon;
he mistakenly believes that there is no Dharma to give to others, taking this to mean the forgetting of the Dharma.

To rely on the single word "forgetting" is nothing other than being reckless and dissolute, brushing aside the essential purpose. To cling to the raft while burning the boat—both are illnesses. Tanji and his ilk are all like this.
It is indeed carried out. It is just like when Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner coming; he gave a shout. The monk also shouted.
Xinghua shouted again. The monk shouted once more. Xinghua said, "Look at this blind fellow! As the monk hesitated, Xinghua struck him directly and drove him out of the Dharma Hall.
The attendant asked, "What did he do to offend him? Huizheng replied, "He too has the provisional and the real.
[Huizheng] then extended his hand across the man's face twice, but the man did not understand. "A blind fellow like this—when shall we wait to strike him?
After Fuguo had finished recounting this, he said, "Behold the authentic style of our school; it is utterly distinct and extraordinary."
One does not prize clever stratagems; one only reveres the correctness of his eye.

To uphold and sustain the orthodox lineage and to maintain the eye of the school, one must penetrate to the very top and the very bottom, through to the bone and to the marrow. Without falling into triviality, one must be utterly liberated and uniquely detached.
Only then can the authentic transmission be maintained, and one may raise this great Dharma banner. Indeed, this great Dharma torch continues the legacy of that master.
The Patriarch Baizhang, Shoushan, and Yangqi did not act out of mere pretension or usurpation. Han Yue, Tanji, and others claimed that one must first penetrate the Dharma and then forget it;
they maintained a gradualist approach, asserting that the ultimate principle is not found in subtle or fragmented attachments, but rather in a state of absolute liberation.
How lamentable that such claims constitute nothing but pretension and usurpation! This old monk’s true character and true function is simply this: [the direct transmission].
The True Eye and the True School—this very section from the Buddha’s Fruit—is likewise intended as my own testimony. It is said:

"The profound essentials, the discernment of guest and host, and the interplay of illumination and function—what a web of complications! How many students have weighed them out and provided commentaries!"

Little do they realize that within the treasury of our King there is no such sword. Furthermore, as I showed my late master Longshu [Lingyun], the Fifth Patriarch was throughout his life solitary and austere;
he rarely gave approval to others. He stood firm and upright like dry wood, relying solely on this one point.
He often said of himself, "It is like leaning against Mount Sumeru; how could I ever fall into emptiness or play with the slippery?"

Deceiving people with their heads held high, they even serve as witnesses for this old monk. Han Yue and his ilk chew on the words and phrases of the ancients, taking them to be the fundamental principle.
This old monk intends to strike them down to the very end with an extremely coarse staff. Thus spoke the Elder Foguo.
This has already been annotated and refuted. If one interprets according to the literal words, one must be given the fodder appropriate to one's own station;
it is like ten *shu* of donkey’s milk—dropping a single drop of lion’s milk into it causes it all to scatter and disperse.
▲ Chan Master Shàolóng of Húqiū in Píngjiāng was a successor of Zhāojié. He was a native of Hánshān in Hézhōu. At the age of nine, he entered the monastic life at Fóhuì Monastery.
Upon reaching maturity, he traveled to study under various masters; he first visited Chán Master Xìn of Chánglú and grasped its general outlines.

Later, when someone brought him a transmission of Fǎguò’s teachings, the Master read them and sighed, saying: "It is like imagining the essence of fermented vinegar; though one has not yet poured it [upon the tongue],..."
It thoroughly washes the stomach and, for the time being, brings one a sense of joy and relief; my only regret is that I have not yet heard your voice.

Thereupon, he proceeded from Baofeng to rely upon Zantang, stayed as a guest at Huanglong, and questioned Chan Master Sishin. Next, he visited Foguo. One day, he entered the inner room, and Foguo asked:
"When seeing the seeing, the seeing is not seeing. Seeing is already apart from seeing; seeing cannot reach it. [Foguo] then raised his fist.

Foguo asked, "Did you see it? The Master said, "I saw it. Foguo said, "That is like placing a head upon a head. Upon hearing this, the Master attained a sudden realization. Foguo rebuked him, saying, "What did you see?
The Master replied, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing stream from passing through. Foguo approved of him and subsequently appointed him to oversee the library.
Someone asked Foguo, "Master Long is so gentle and easygoing; how can he achieve anything? Foguo—
It is said: "A dozing tiger.
Yanming was Chan Master Ying’an Tanhua of Tiantong in Mingzhou; he was a successor of Huqiu and the son of the Jiang family of Qizhou.
From birth, he was extraordinary and did not resemble ordinary children. At the age of seventeen, he went to Dongchan to receive the tonsure and first visited Suhe.

Furthermore, having briefly gained a taste of the flavor of the Dharma, he traveled extensively to consult various spiritual teachers (*kalyāṇamitra*), yet found nothing that accorded with his realization.

Hearing that Foguo resided at Yunju and rigorously tempered his disciples, the Master went there to pay his respects and attend upon him. Foguo subjected him to intense scrutiny and piercing interrogation.

When Foguo returned to Shu, he was directed to visit Chan Master Long of Huqiu. He attended him for one year and suddenly attained clear understanding of the Great Matter. Thereafter, he sought this [teacher].
An Yuan ordered that he be given a seat beside him. Thereupon, Miaoyan opened the hall for formal teaching and moved to Guiyang. At that time, Dahui was at Mei Yang;
when a monk brought him a record of the Master’s address to the assembly, Dahui saw it and praised it with great fervor. He further sent a verse, saying:
"Severing the path atop the First Peak of the Golden Wheel, A thousand demons and a hundred monsters all hide their traces. In recent years, I have finally received the true news."
The report states that Yangqi’s true lineage was transmitted; at that time, he and Dahui were both called the "Two Gates of Ambrosia.
[A critic] said: "Regarding the Great Dharma of Linji, there have been those in later generations who attained its 'self-enjoyment,' though they were few.
As for 'driving the plow and seizing the food' and 'untying the sticky and removing the bonds,' from Yinyuan, Huazang, and those below them, there has not yet been one capable of explaining it."

It must necessarily be put into practice. Yet those who can use it may not necessarily be able to use it fully; there may be aspects that remain unexamined due to exhaustion, or that are treated superficially rather than with precision.
For this reason, the various masters of the past no longer brought it forth. In recent times, the core teachings (zongzhi) have consequently come to be regarded as strange and absurd;
this is truly the result of a gradual process reaching its culmination. In my "Rescue of the Five Schools" (Wuzongjiu), I shall certainly record both the gains and losses.

I do not distort what I have heard to argue against the former masters; for the flourishing or decline of the Dharma depends upon this. If you know this and yet condemn me, what cause for regret could there be?
Han Yue arbitrarily fabricated a "one" (○) as the ancestor of the thousand Buddhas and ten thousand Buddhas, claiming that each of the five houses emerged from one aspect of this "one.
If that were so, even Linji would be bound and fettered by this "one."

Furthermore, by employing numerous entanglements to bind Linji and taking that as his primary tenet, he has obliterated the orthodox eye and the true lineage transmitted from of old, establishing himself as a heterodox outsider. How can this not be called strange and absurd?
Tanji composed the *Wujiongjiu* (Rescue of the Five Houses), relying on what he heard from Han-yueh to evaluate the former masters; it was not merely to "follow his father."
This is to oppose Zuoyi. It will not allow the four characters [of the "Four-Word"] to be raised again; it will erase Tianqi and the various patriarchs.

It implies that those who can speak may not necessarily be able to act, and those who can act may not necessarily be able to act fully—these two phrases erase all the patriarchs from Ying'an and Huazang downward.
Little do they realize that the fundamental principle of Linji is utterly transcendent and unique, leaving nothing behind.
The Dharma and the person: the various patriarchs possessed these as the True Eye; they inherited them as the True Lineage.
Without waiting for the driving away of oxen or the seizing of food, the plowman remains a plowman, and the hungry man remains a hungry man.

Free and at ease, uniquely liberated and without dependence, there is directly beneath one nothing sticky to be untied and no bond to be removed. How could there be another separate dharma to bestow upon people?

This is truly about "untying the sticky and removing the bonds. It means that, based on the *svasaṃbhogakāya* (self-enjoyment body), one directly points to all people so that each may awaken to their own self-enjoyment; this is precisely what it is.

Although there have been those among the successive patriarchs following Ying’an who slandered [the teaching], claiming that those who attain the *svasaṃbhogakāya* are few and that the school's tenets are strange and absurd, this was actually due to a gradual descent into superficiality.

Seeing the Way of Fenyang, one clearly grasps the intent of the ancients; its transformations are sovereign and its application inexhaustible—this is called the Body of Self-Enjoyment (*svasaṃbhogakāya*).
How could there be a self-enjoyment attained by one who does not clarify the fundamental principle?
And how could there be one who clarifies the fundamental principle yet fails to attain self-enjoyment? Indeed, a monk of true character abides in this very Body of Self-Enjoyment.
Standing far apart and uniquely liberated, he directly points out all people using the fodder of their own fundamental portion, so that each may awaken to their own self-experience;
he bestows no other dharma upon anyone. This is precisely the essential teaching of Linji;
this is precisely Linji’s “beating the bone to extract the marrow” and his “driving in the awl with painful force. It is like driving the ox of the plowman and seizing the food of the hungry man.
Tanjí has never once awakened to these means. Relying on what he heard from Han Yue, he composed the *Wuzongjiu* (Rescue of the Five Schools) to rescue the origins of the Five Schools;
yet he recklessly treated the essential tenets as personal property, splitting them into two separate parts.
He shackled the former sages and obliterated his own ancestors. Alas! This is precisely why he is considered so strange and preposterous. This is what [he has done].
[The people] considered him strange and eccentric.
▲ Chan Master Mian Xianjie of Tiantong in Mingzhou was a successor of Ying’an. He was the son of the Zheng family of Fuzhou.

His mother dreamed that an old monk from Mount Lu entered her home, and subsequently gave birth to the Master. From childhood, he was exceptionally brilliant and surpassed others; by the time he reached adulthood, he had shaved his head [in ordination].

Having received full ordination, he traveled extensively to visit various spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*). Finally, he went to Mingguo Monastery in Quzhou to pay his respects to Master Ying’an Hua.
One day, Ying’an asked him, “What is the True Dharma Eye? He replied, “A broken sandpot. Ying’an nodded in approval.

He spoke in verse: "The phrase of great penetration that hits the mark, Directly opens up the crown of the head. Now, for four years, we have followed him; His probing questions leave no trace behind.
Though he has not yet handed over the bowl and robe, His spirit and bearing swallow the heavens and earth. Yet he takes the Eye of the True Dharma And calls it a broken sand-pot.
Later, he appeared in the world and resided at Wugu in Quzhou. Subsequently, he moved to Jiangshan Huazang in Xiangfu. Not long after...
For several years, he served by imperial decree at Mount Jing and Lingyin Monasteries.
Tanji, citing Mian’s discourse on ascending the hall, struck his staff once and said: "When deluded, one is deluded only regarding this very thing."

He struck the floor once more and said: "When awakening occurs, one awakens only to this very thing. When both delusion and awakening are forgotten, it is like adding another basket to a pile of refuse.
Is there anyone who, at the point where the whole mechanism is uniquely liberated—where the east surges up and the west sinks down—can utter a single word?
If you cannot, Huazang will speak for himself. He threw down his staff and said: "Thirty!"

Three years later, Jiù said: "The典刑 (diǎn xíng) still remains. I, the old monk, look upon these four characters, "the典刑 still remains," and see them as words of insufficiency—meaning, as it is said: "Though there be no more elders of experience, the典刑 still remain.
Tánjì often spoke of the Mind-Seal of the Patriarchs, which was transmitted from Língjì to Yìngān through twelve generations; after Huázàng, this...
The seal gradually vanishes. I do not know what evidence there is for this. Take, for instance, the path of Mitan:
is there anyone who can utter a single phrase regarding the state of total liberation, where one emerges from the east and sinks in the west? Tanji, try and speak it!
If you cannot grasp it, do not slander Mian.

Upon arriving at Lingyin, Chan Master Puan was serving as the First Seat (Dizhuo). One day, while touring Shisun Hermitage, the Master...

▲ Chan Master Xueyan Zuqin of Yangshan was a successor of Wuzhun. Initially, the Master studied under Tiejue Yuan; subsequently, he studied under Tianmu Li.

One day, as soon as he sat upon his meditation mat, everything before him suddenly opened up, as if the earth had collapsed beneath him. From that point on—
This present moment is pure and starkly naked; for more than half a month, no signs of movement have arisen.
Yet, during the middle watch of the night, while fast asleep in a state where there is no dreaming, no thinking, no hearing, and no seeing, it is once again split into two pieces.

Only when things are thus similar can one finally see where the Old Man of Jingshan stands; he deserves exactly thirty blows of the staff.
▲ Chan Master Gaofeng Yuanmiao of Tianmu was a successor of Xueyan. He was the son of the Xu family of Wujiang. At fifteen, he left home at Miyin Temple in Xiushui.

"I have already failed to accomplish my own affairs; how much better it would be to assist him until his success is achieved. Thereupon, he attended upon him morning and evening with the utmost diligence.

There was not a single day that passed without this occurring. One day, Yanguan suddenly asked, "Who gave you this dead corpse to drag around?
