Tiantong Jiu said:

"The Master’s character is upright and firm, and his merit and virtue are likewise great. In his conduct regarding the matters of leaving and staying as abbot, he truly embodies the standards of the ancients.
This is something I have heard of and been moved by for several years, such that my heart was intoxicated with admiration and my mind was in full submission."
When his family was poor and he lost the opportunity for study, he carried his burden through the wilds and grasses of remote mountains.
His mind was filled with a restless yearning, his resolve set upon transcending the world. Were it not for a great vow made in a former life, who could have taught him or caused him to become thus?

Although there may be no regrets even as small as a hair or a speck regarding the matters of the Buddhas and Patriarchs since time immemorial, as for this "self-acceptance," it is truly attained only by seeing the One Face directly.
This is by no means something that can be glimpsed or fathomed by those who have recently acquired learning or attained supernatural powers through meditative absorption.
Had figures such as Fenyang and Ciming been his teachers and friends, they would surely have been able to revive the Linji lineage in this degenerate age and erect the great banner of the Dharma;
their merit would have been immeasurable. I, the old monk, shall now ask Tanji: why do you not point directly to Fenyang and Ciming?
If you come here to expose the old monk’s shortcomings, then it may be seen that you possess the eye of discernment regarding the Dharma.

Otherwise, you are merely speaking empty falsehoods and confused nonsense. To falsely claim that Fenyang and Ciming have come to cover for the old monk is not only a slander against me and a loss of the strength of your teachers and friends, but it is also a slander against my late master;
such people are unworthy of being models, and they are likewise slandering [the Buddhas and patriarchs].
To slander Fenyang Wuye and Ciming is to misunderstand them. Why? When the old monk was present, Fenyang rebuked Ciming, saying, "This is a wicked teacher!
How dare you deceive and exploit me? He raised his staff to drive him away. As Ciming prepared to offer a defense, Fenyang covered his mouth.
Ciming attained great enlightenment and said, "Now I know that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiments. Thus, how could it have been Fenyang who... [was at fault]?
Is there a Dharma that is clear through loving-kindness? Again, according to Fenyang, he studied under more than seventy spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*).
Later, he visited Shoushan and asked, "What is the meaning of Baizhang’s folding the mat? Shoushan said, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed.
[Fenyang] asked, "What is your own meaning, Master? Shoushan said, "Where the Elephant King walks, there are no traces of foxes. Yang said, "Ten thousand..."
The ancient emerald pool, the void of the sky, and the moon: only after repeatedly searching and grappling with them will one finally come to know them.
Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that you were so spontaneously convinced? Yang said, "This is precisely where I surrendered my body and life. This was Fen-yang.
How could there ever have been a separate dharma obtained at Shoushan?

You, on the contrary, claim that figures such as Fenyang Wuye and Ciming Fazhen were able to serve as teachers and friends who would surely cause the Linji lineage to flourish once more in the末代 (mòdài—final age). But let me ask you:
what do you designate as the "final age," and what do you designate as the "banner of the Dharma"? According to this old monk, as for the world...
Without beginning or end, he directly points to all people to act as the Dharma Banner themselves; this Dharma Banner is likewise inexhaustible.

If one were to establish some other profound or essential Dharma Banner, claiming to revive Linji in the末法 (mofa) age, that would be slandering the True Wheel of Dharma—what merit could there be in that?
Furthermore, Shoushan himself said: "Where the Elephant King walks, foxes have no place."
Zongzhi and Han-yue are wild fox spirits; they, in turn, slander this old monk as being "a single block of hard Zen. Tanji and Yi are also wild fox spirits;
they, in turn, slander this old monk regarding the matters handed down from of old, claiming there is not even a hair’s breadth of regret left behind.
Now, let me ask you all: what do you call the matters handed down from of old? Is it the three strikes on the pestle, or the three jars of wine?
"Pickled sauce. Three blows of the staff for a meal. Are the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials that have been transmitted matters from of old?
Is it not so that before King Wei-yin, beyond form and sound, there was nothing yet recorded and no basis for verification?
That "one circle" (○) is the ancestor of the thousand Buddhas and ten thousand Buddhas, and that each of the Five Houses emerged from one aspect of that circle—is this from of old?
How so? Such views of these wild fox spirits are not enough to withstand a single trampling by this old monk, the Great Elephant King.
The Zen Master Miyun Yuanwu of Tiantong, Mingzhou, was a successor of Longchi. He was the son of the Jiang family of Yixing.
His family was poor, and he made his living as a woodcutter. However, during two or three months each year, he would suddenly be moved by the impermanence of the world.
He conceived this thought and immediately desired to practice. At the age of twenty-seven, while carrying a load across a mountain, he encountered a bend in the path where firewood was piled;
at that moment, he attained a realization. He gained mastery over his mind and, in his daily life, constantly maintained a state of luminous clarity. Two years later, he abandoned his household life.
The following year, he left home under the guidance of Chan Master Hanyou Chuan of Longchi Mountain. Thereupon, he became fully aware that the arrival of birth and death was imminent.

In the end, it was not stable. Throughout the twelve periods of the day and night, I observed that the mind and its objects remained as two distinct entities. An ancient said, "Heaven and earth share the same root;
the myriad things are one body. Yet, the more I looked, the more they appeared as two. Consequently, while traveling by boat, I requested instruction from Longchi. Longchi said:

"If you reach this state," he said, "then simply let your body lie down. When the Master rose from his prostration, his confusion became even more profound. From then on, [Nanquan] did nothing but hurl insults at him.
The Master was overcome by a mixture of shame and distress until he fell gravely ill and broke into a sweat; it was only after fourteen days that he recovered.
He subsequently remained in seclusion behind closed doors for several years. It happened that when Master Quan entered the capital, he appointed the Master to oversee the affairs of the monastery.
One day, returning from the city, he passed the summit of Mount Tongguan. Suddenly, he realized that the sentient and the insentient were manifest as equal and uniform.

He sought even the slightest fault or affliction but could find none; in general, it was impossible to describe it to others. At that moment, that which was "brightly clear and spiritually aware" suddenly sought to arise.
He arose and could not return; though he sought him, he could not find him, for he did not know where he had gone.

Furthermore, he privately and repeatedly brought to mind the ancient precedents he had previously encountered, which were entirely different from this case; yet he did not doubt whether they were the same or not.
One day, Longchi summoned the Master. When Jueyu entered the room, Longchi said, "Last night I got up and took a walk;
I have the handle of things entirely in my hands. You all must support the Buddha-dharma for me. The Master then departed and presented this verse:
"If I, this humble one, were to support the Buddha-dharma, I would let him [Longchi] do whatever he pleases. As for everything that comes before us, I give it all back to him."
"Thirty blows! Do not say that this was clearly for the purpose of rewarding or punishing. Longchi looked at him and laughed heartily. The Master received [the body] and committed it to the flames.
Not long after, Master Chuan passed away. After accompanying the coffin for three years, the Master entered the formal retreat (jie) at his home mountain.
At that time, he was fifty-two years old.
Tánjì cites the writings of Huìpì, saying: "When Hányuè first met me, he asked about the inner sanctum (táng-ào).
I replied, 'Where are you right now? He, however, failed to recognize my words, claiming they were still merely matters of the outer gate (mén-tíng).
Is this not wandering outside the door, failing to recognize the inner sanctum of Hányuè?"
Is this not the matter at hand? Why? The innermost depth is where the host rests; it is the very ground upon which the moon stands.

When I, a poor monk, take up the ground where the moon stands, yet the moon moves outward, striking and circling about—could this not be because one’s karmic consciousness is vast and wandering, having no fundamental basis to rely upon? Furthermore, it is said: "As when a poor monk throws [it]..."
[The Master] lowered his staff and said, "The old monk has already fallen twice. As for 'the first,' how would you raise it?
Han Yue stepped forward, seized the staff, and walked away. Is this not another instance where Han Yue failed to recognize the old monk’s point of application?
[The Master] alone rejoiced and looked at him, saying, "Since it is after the moon has set, how will you interact with me?"
He saw [the master] and then went out; thus, he used the whisk as a symbol of his transmission. Jiuzhuo said:
"I would rather cast my body into hell than treat the Buddha-Dharma as a matter of personal favor. This was the self-vow of an ancient worthy.
If we follow the arguments in the *Pibushu*, then the former master neither knew his own standing ground nor recognized the lifting [of the whisk].
To claim that "one utterance contains two functions" is merely the hollow talk of a man who is utterly ignorant and devoid of understanding.
To take a single instance and, out of mere personal preference, present it as the ultimate source and lineage—does this not treat the life-blood of the Buddhas and patriarchs as a child’s play?
Furthermore, it is not only our late master who acted thus; several others to whom the Dharma was transmitted did the same.
You immediately affirm what preceded and deny what followed. Where, then, is the pure Dharma-eye?

You fail to consider that it was precisely because I sought the pure Dharma-eye that I alone took delight in producing this one matter, transmitting the lineage for the sake of the Buddhas' and Patriarchs' life-force of wisdom.
Why is this? If one were to rely solely on the production of this one matter, how could there be any further inner sanctum?
Yes. Could there be yet another gateway? Furthermore, could it be that the staff is used merely as a single illustration?

Moreover, could it be said that when artists depict the origins of the Seven Buddhas—beginning with Vipaśyin Buddha (Viyūṇarāja)—they first draw a large circle (*maṇḍala*) as a perfect symbol, and only thereafter do the Seven Buddhas each have their own verbal expressions? Although these verbal expressions differ, all [the Buddhas]...
Is not the purport of the Buddha’s verses nothing other than the manifestation of the Perfect Phase (*yuanxiang*)?

Furthermore, could it be said that "awe" (*wei*) exists outside of form, and "sound" (*yin*) exists outside of voice? If so, would there be no record or basis for the existence of the King of Awe-Sound (*Weiyinwang*) beyond both form and voice?
According to Han Yue, "awe" is indeed outside of form and "sound" is outside of voice; though this is the Way...

Throughout the life of Han Yue, whether he held up his whisk, raised his bamboo staff, spoke in the hall, or took up the pen to write—indeed, in all his daily activities—he was never apart from the form and sound of Han Yue.
This is because Han Yue failed to follow the principle of "producing one matter directly," instead giving rise to various confused theories and actions to slander this old monk. Thus, the old monk...

As for the Sangha member who was right in the beginning but wrong in the end—namely Han Yue—it was because he was right at first and then became wrong that he brought trouble upon the Old Monk, leading to this being opened up once and then again.
To open it up directly to the very end is for no other reason than the desire to rectify Han Yue and cause him to know the matter of those who have come before us:
"This one reality alone is the truth; the other two are not real. Furthermore, in his attempt to save [Han Yue], he also said:
I once read a case concerning Master Dongshan’s examination of a monk, which bears a striking resemblance to this.
Dongshan asked a monk, “What is your name? The monk replied, “This one. Dongshan said, “Who is that master of yours? The monk replied, “The one who is currently responding.
Dongshan said, “Alas, alas! People of the present age are all like this; they recognize only the front of the donkey.”
To take the horse’s hindquarters as one's own is precisely what causes the Buddha-dharma to sink into oblivion.
When the guest within has not yet been distinguished, how can one discern the host within the host? A monk then asked, "What is the host within the host?
Shishuang said, "The *ācārya* should speak for yourself. The monk said, "If I were to speak it, that would merely be the guest within the host. What then is..."
"Lord of Lords," the Master said, "To speak in such a manner is easy; to maintain continuity is most difficult. He then presented this verse: "Alas!
I see the practitioners of the Way nowadays, By the thousands and tens of thousands, who merely recognize the gateway.

They are just like those entering the capital to pay court to the Holy Sovereign, Who stop as soon as they reach Tongguan Pass. The former Master asked about the matters within the inner sanctum, And [the disciples] replied:"
"Where are you right now? He then explained it himself, saying: "The character 'āo' (奥) refers to the place where the master rests;
that is the very spot where I stand. Is this not to say that this monk and I share the same nostrils?
The old monk said: "This monk indeed shares the same nostrils as Han Yue Tanji. Why? Simply because, according to the [Linji] lineage..."
Mount [Wutai] says that thousands upon thousands and tens of thousands recognize the gatehead; yet Han Yue does not recognize the Old Monk.

Mount directly points to the place where Han Yue stands, yet he conversely claims this is still merely a matter at the edge of the gate. Is it not that he recognizes only the gatehead and fails to recognize Han Yue?
Furthermore, when the Old Monk points to him and says, "Sit for now," is this not once again pointing to Han Yue himself as the master? It is exactly the same.
Dongshan’s so-called “Does the *śrāmaṇera* speak for himself?”—Tan Ji does not recognize the pulse of ancient and modern discourse.

and thus further slanders me by claiming I said to a certain monk, “This is the host within the guest,” and then questioned Dongshan.
Shan: "What is the Lord of Lords? [The other] replied, "We share the same nostrils. Is this not the height of perversity?
Dongshan’s verse says: "Alas, I see the practitioners of the Way nowadays, Countless millions who merely recognize the gate."
It is just like entering the capital to pay court to the Holy Lord, yet stopping as soon as one reaches Tongguan Pass.
Now, Han Yue takes up his staff and departs; he recognizes only the staff. When has he ever recognized Han Yue himself as the Master?
Is this not the same nostril as those who "never reached the capital to see the face of the Holy Lord," rather than merely reaching Tongguan Pass? (Jiù)
In the middle [section] he further states: My late master once composed a verse on the first three cases, saying: "Raising one, raising two—these are the words of the Patriarch himself.

To say that the one who correctly answers for this monk is the "host within the guest," yet conversely pushes the "host within the host" back into the realm of Dongshan’s classification, is to share the same nostril [with him].
Tanji laments that those who uphold the ancestral Way have caused such confusion.
It is all the more laughable that those who study the family [of Chan] fail to understand after three rounds of casting the dice.
Han Yue, Tanji, and others do not rely on their own realization to uphold the ancestral Way; instead, they trace it back to the state of an old monk.
Yet the old monk clearly pointed at Han Yue and asked, "Where are you right now? Han Yue did not know, and took this to be a mere matter of gatekeeping—a grave error.
"Clearly manifesting the Han Moon, he himself casts the Han Moon as his gateway. For Han Moon to cast the Han Moon is to miss the mark regarding the Han Moon;

that is to miss the mark regarding this old monk as well. Therefore, the old monk again pointed at Han Moon and told him to sit, and then struck Han Moon, driving him straight out of the abbot’s quarters.
This was a direct, face-to-face holding up of the Dharma, a total manifestation of function. How many times did Han Moon [miss it]?"
To miss the mark without realizing it—is this not what Linji meant when he said, "I function with my whole being;
if a student blinks their eyes, they have already missed it"? Furthermore, in the *Jiujue* (Rescue), it is said:

Someone may doubt this, saying, "If Sanfeng considers that person to be one who does not recognize the fundamental tenet (*zongzhi*), then he should simply not have received the lineage transmission (*yuanliu*). Yet, since he has already received it..."

As for its origins and developments, why should there be so much debate and discussion? This is simply because one has failed to examine the hearts of those who propagate the Dharma and remedy its deficiencies.
Now, when Confucius served in Lu and Mencius traveled to Liang, it was not that they sought to sell their teachings.

It is solely for the purpose of elucidating the Way of Yao and Shun. How could those sages and worthies have treated the rulers of Liang and Lu as their equals to Yao and Shun, only thereafter serving them as ministers? They merely hoped to be able to discourse upon the Way of Yao and Shun.
Now, when one's words are not employed, one simply departs; yet they depart and are forbidden, being told: "Do not lose this man for the rest of your life."

The rites of a minister are within the capacity of a man of middle rank. Yet you distance yourself from them and prohibit them, saying, "Never speak of the Way of Yao and Shun for the rest of your life.
Even Confucius and Mencius could not have achieved this; that you, unable to do so, should instead suppress it—do you not feel a sense of lamentation?
The way the Three Peaks receive their source and stream is just like how Confucius and Mencius served the states of Liang and Lu.

The Master [Zhuangzi] was likewise a sovereign who did not find favor with his subjects; the Three Peaks (Sanfeng) did not find favor with their teacher, just as Confucius and Mencius did not find favor with the feudal lords.
In antiquity, when a minister failed to find favor with his ruler, or a son failed to find favor with his father, the Way reached its limit.
Some then composed books to clarify their intentions, while others wrote poems to express their grief and resentment. [The "Little Bow" (Xiāobàn)]... [separated].
The *Sao* (Songs of the South) is an example of such works. Our late Master Sanfeng rectified the fundamental principles of a hundred generations;

his language was lofty and his spirit was resolute as he praised antiquity and censured the present. This was truly intended to clarify the way between superior and inferior, ensuring it would not fall into ruin.
Yet, did he alone avoid offending against taboos? Confucius once composed the *Spring and Autumn Annals*; I, an old monk, certainly have never done so.
Regarding the study of the texts: it is based on what Confucius said to Zengzi: "Zhen, my Way is one that runs through everything.
Zengzi replied, "Yes. His disciples did not understand this, so Zengzi said, "The Master’s Way is simply loyalty and reciprocity."
Zhu Xi’s commentary states that "exhausting oneself" is loyalty (*zhong*) and "extending oneself" is benevolence (*shu*). Yet Han Yue, outside of the self, arbitrarily fabricates a circle (○);
is this not a reversal of the Way of the One Thread (*yiguan*) of Laozi? Mencius said, "The physical form and its colors are the nature of Heaven.
Yet Han Yue points to "awe" as being outside of form and "sound" as being outside of voice; is this not a reversal of Mencius’s doctrine of the nature of Heaven?
This is the Way. Han Yue has reversed the Way of Confucius and Mencius; he speaks recklessly of Yao and Shun and imitates the *Spring and Autumn Annals* with arrogance.

He fails to consider that when Confucius composed the *Spring and Autumn*, it was specifically for the sake of rebellious ministers and treacherous sons, and when Mencius refuted Yang Zhu and Mo Di, it was specifically for the sake of those who lack filial piety and loyalty to their sovereign.
As for Han Yue, Tan Ji, and their ilk now attempting to erase this old monk, there is no need to speak further.
Furthermore, because he was unable to serve as a model, he sought to erase his predecessor; because he had not yet escaped haste, he sought to erase Xiangyan;
because he remained stuck in the flow of conventional language, he sought to erase Wumen; because the word "who" tainted his grasp, he sought to erase Tianqi;
and he even wished to erase the two patriarchs Baozang and Dongming, claiming that the lineage of Longchi was erroneous, tracing it back further...
To speak of "resonance" (xiangzi) with the Way is to erase Qianyan; to sweep away the fundamental principle (zongzhi) is to erase Zhongfeng;
to apply the blade and administer the medicine is to leave a gap between oneself and the ancients;

to erase Xueyan and his disciples is because one may be able to speak but not necessarily able to act, and may be able to act but not necessarily able to act fully; this erases everyone from Ying’an and Huazang downward.
Among the various patriarchs of successive dynasties, there is one who is particularly remarkable:
taking Miaoxi as the foremost disciple who truly grasped the intent of Foguo, yet he utterly eclipsed my own Huqiu Long. His total destruction of his ancestral lineage reached such an extreme.

Among the gentlemen of the world who have studied the classics, and the eminent scholars who clarify the principles of truth, they would consider that such a person could not escape the brush of the "rebellious sons" whom Confucius and Mencius condemned.
[The opponent] objects: "Is not the mouth of one who lacks a father to be condemned? You merely compare [the *Zhao lun*] to the *Xiaoban* and the *Li sao* based on its impassioned tone and rhetoric;
this is but a fabrication of falsehoods. In response, it is said: One day the Sixth Patriarch addressed the assembly, saying:
"I have an object that has no head and no tail, no name and no character, no back and no front. Do you all recognize it?"
Shenhui stepped forward and said, "This is the original source of all Buddhas; it is Shenhui’s own Buddha-nature.
The Patriarch said, "I told you that it has no name and no character, yet you immediately call it 'the original source' and 'Buddha-nature.

In the future, even if you cover your head with a bundle of thatch, you will still remain nothing more than a follower of the school of intellectual understanding. This is the original teaching from Caoxi. As I observe it...
The school of the Plucking Flower has flowed to China; from the First Patriarch to the Sixth Patriarch, each had collateral lineages.

It was appropriate that Master Hui [Nanquan Puyuan] rejected the calculation of the original source of Buddha-nature upon the basis of namelessness and wordlessness as being merely intellectual understanding (*jiejie*).

For this reason, the five houses each established their own school tenets specifically to treat this malady of intellectual understanding; it was not out of loathing for the former or attachment to the latter.
This is a new [approach]. For example, when a monk asked Yunmen, "What is the place where all Buddhas are born?
he replied, "On the water above the mountain to the east. When a monk asked Dongshan, "What is the Buddha? he replied, "Three pounds of flax.
Linji said, "Within a single phrase are contained the three mysteries; within each mystery are contained the three essentials. If it is thus, then this is the fundamental Buddha-nature.
How could intellectual understanding possibly give rise to it? Now, you open your book and establish a "school of principles" based on intellectual understanding;
this is contrary to the words of the Sixth Patriarch. Relying on the single character "original" (yuan), I, this old monk, designate you as a follower of the school of intellectual understanding.
This indeed does not contradict the words of the Sixth Patriarch. Why is this? "Original" (*yuan*) means to trace back to the origin.
Han Yue traced back the origins of how the five houses established their respective *zong* (doctrinal principles), composing the *Wuzongyuan* (The Origins of the Five Houses).

This precisely accords with Shenhui’s tracing back to the origin of the Sixth Patriarch’s words, asserting that they constitute the fundamental source of all Buddhas and the Buddha-nature of Shenhui; both are identical in their tracing back to the origin.

Cecheng Tanji said: "It is certainly appropriate to condemn Master Hui for calculating the original source of Buddha-nature at the level of 'namelessness' as mere intellectual understanding (*zhijie*).

However, when Han Yue traced back the origins of how the Five Houses were established prior to their existence, why would the Old Monk’s condemnation of this as intellectual understanding not also be inappropriate? You further state that each of the five houses...
To establish a "school tenet" (*zongzhi*) is specifically to treat this disease of intellectual understanding. The Old Monk says:

if one claims that each of the five houses established its own school tenet, one has already produced the intellectual understanding of "each of the five houses establishing its own school tenet" upon that which is nameless.
How much more so when one claims to "specifically treat this disease of intellectual understanding"—is this not treating the intellectual understanding *of* intellectual understanding? Furthermore...

Furthermore, you claim that because there is no weariness, there is still novelty; because there is existence, there is novelty; that there is weariness and there is stillness; and that there is right and there is wrong.

Do you really possess such a wealth of intellectual understanding? As for citing the monk’s question to Yunmen—“What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?”—and Yunmen’s reply, “On the water above the East Mountain,” it may seem as though Yunmen did not give rise to intellectual understanding. However, this is merely so.
One does not perceive the path to the fruit of Buddhahood. Tianning did not act in this way. If someone were to ask, "What is the place where all Buddhas emerge?
he would simply say to them: "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool.

Is this not because he feared people would fall into the trap of seeking it by walking on water atop Dongshan, thereby creating conceptual nests and generating intellectual interpretations? Once again, he raised the case of a monk’s question.
Dongshan was asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "Three pounds of hemp. This is said because Dongshan did not give rise to intellectual understanding;
this seems to be the case as well. Did you not see Wuzu Yan’s saying, "A fellow carrying a shoulder-pole who sells cheap hemp"?
And did you not see Yungai Zhi’s saying, "Dongshan’s 'three pounds of hemp' is clearly missing one move"? Is this not because he feared people would [cling to the words]?

"Three *jin* of hemp" (the title of the case). They have fashioned a nest and a mortar; do they possess innate understanding? As for what Linji said—"In a single phrase there are three mysteries (*xuan*);
in each mystery there are three essentials (*yao*)"—Tan Ji and others interpreted this as referring to actual dharmas.

Having already reckoned the names of the "three mysteries and three essentials" upon that which is nameless and characterless, they have searched everywhere throughout ancient and modern times for these three dharmas.
It is like the three strikes on the pestle, the three jars of sauce, or the three shakes of the door-panel; these are fixed as "deadly" or "fatal" [kōans].
How could such perverse knowledge and perverse understanding be limited merely to those who follow the school of intellectual understanding?

You cite Yunmen’s “walking on water on East Mountain,” Dongshan’s “three pounds of flax,” and Linji’s statement that “within one phrase there are three mysteries, and within each mystery... [and so forth].
Though you possess the three essentials, you have not given rise to the knowledge and understanding of the original source, Buddha-nature.

It is not only Shenhui whom I reject for his conceptual understanding; I likewise reject the Sixth Patriarch’s statement, "I have a thing which has no head and no tail, no name and no character, no back and no front," and so forth, because it gives rise to the conceptual understanding of original source Buddha-nature. You yourself are merely creating dualistic discrimination.
One naturally gives rise to understanding; how can it be said that the words of Yunmen, Dongshan, and Linji do not give rise to understanding, while the words of the Sixth Patriarch can?

According to your claim that establishing a school’s tenets through polemical writings constitutes understanding, this contradicts the words of the Sixth Patriarch. I, this old monk, do not approve of Han Yue. At—
Before the five schools existed, one must trace them back to the origins of their respective tenets.
This is precisely like the Sixth Patriarch’s refusal to permit Shen-hui to trace the original source of Buddha-nature back to that which is nameless and characterless;

for this reason, the Sixth Patriarch rebuked Shen-hui as a follower of the school of intellectual understanding (*jiejie zongtu*). I, too, likewise rebuke Han-yue as a follower of the school of intellectual understanding.
Fool! How could there be any contradiction within this? Why trouble yourself with Tanji, only to give rise once more to a contradictory understanding?
According to you, regarding the single school of "Plucking the Flower," those four characters immediately give rise to intellectual understanding from the very outset.

When the World-Honored One held up a flower, when did he ever establish "holding up a flower" as the fundamental tenet? In years past, I once composed a verse: "The World-Honored One’s entire being was elegant;
Kāśyapa’s whole person was peddling charm. At that time, among the hundreds of thousands of devas and humans, they saw only the holding up of the flower and the smile.
You say: how does this verse of mine compare to the Sixth Patriarch’s ‘I have a thing...’?"

Are they the same or different? According to your claim that from the First Patriarch down to the Sixth Patriarch there were all those who branched out, it is just like the case of the Second Patriarch’s branch, Master Sengna, who once instructed people, saying: "To further add mental characteristics deeply violates the Buddha's intent;
to increase discursive arguments is utterly contrary to the Great Principle. Is this not a refusal to allow people to give rise to intellectual understanding? Thus...

Regarding the story of how the hundred birds brought flowers to Ox Head before he had seen the Fourth Patriarch, but after seeing him, the hundred birds no longer brought flowers—where can the two words "knowledge" and "understanding" be established? Consider this: A monk asked Zhaozhou, "How was it before Ox Head saw the Fourth Patriarch?
He replied, "Sufficient firewood, sufficient water. [The monk asked,] "How was it after he saw him? He replied, "Sufficient firewood, sufficient water."

Water—how could it allow you to give rise to intellectual understanding? It is just like when the Fifth Patriarch’s collateral descendant, Zen Master Hui’an of Mount Song, was conversing hand-in-hand with the Duke of Wan-hui; though those standing by listened intently, they did not grasp a single word.
How could there be any further intellectual understanding to be produced? Furthermore, National Teacher Zhong of Nanyang attained the Dharma at Caoxi, yet his own body...

The mind is a single suchness; there is nothing else outside the body. The lands of the ten directions are all the body of Vairocana Buddha—such words sweep away the conceptual nests of seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing. Thus, Miaoxi once said:
"Do you think the National Teacher was preaching 'old lady Chan,' muddying the waters? How could one possibly chew upon mere words and phrases? It is precisely for this reason that he said:
"Can the National Teacher produce intellectual understanding? From this perspective, prior to the emergence of the Five Houses, there was originally no production of intellectual understanding;
how could it have waited for each of the five schools to establish its own doctrine? Yunmen said, "The water flows atop the Eastern Mountain.
Dongshan said, "Three pounds of flax. Linji said, "Within a single phrase, the Three Mysteries are contained. One...
"Within the profound mystery, the three essentials are fully present; only then does one know that conceptual understanding does not arise. Tanzhi Ji said:

"From the First Patriarch to the Sixth Patriarch, there were all those who branched out from the main line. Master Hui directed his attention toward the nameless and characterless state, calculating the original source of Buddha-nature."

It is entirely appropriate to reject [the pursuit of] intellectual understanding. For this reason, the five houses each established their own school tenets specifically to treat this disease of intellectual understanding.
You, however, because of your intellectual understanding derived from Shenhui, have become a heterodox offshoot; you then proceed to falsely accuse those who are heterodox.

They are all merely followers of the school of intellectual understanding (*jiejie*). Take, for instance, Guo Yi Qin, Songshan Gui, and other great masters such as Po-zao and Niaoke—how can they be dismissed en masse with the two words "intellectual understanding"?

How could one claim that each of the Five Houses established its own school tenet solely to cultivate this derivative intellectual understanding? It was because of Han Yue’s grasping at a staff that the old monk [spoke thus].
Being able to attain liberation alone and without reliance, there subsequently arose the theory of "deviant departure" (*pángchū*).

Because Han Yue sent the *Wǔzōngyuán* (The Source of the Five Houses), the single character "source" (*yuán*) therein led to the theory of the "sect of intellectual understanding" (*zhījiě zōngtú*). These were all expedient medicines for a specific occasion;
they were not intended to correspond with one another from beginning to end. Furthermore, at that time, although he received the *Wǔzōngyuán*, he never actually read it.
It is merely because of the single character "yuan" (source/origin) in the title that [the author] has said such things. However, judging by today’s standards, this is nothing less than heterodoxy;
how can it be called a mere "collateral branch"? It is truly a wild fox spirit; how can it be called a follower of the school of intellectual understanding?
Tan Ji then states: "This book appeared in the third year of the Chongzhen era. The *Qibai* (Seven Refutations) appeared in..."
Seven years later, it was published in the ninth year [of the Kangxi era]. Master Mǐn wrote a preface for it, stating:
"This is a refutation of the writings of Master Hányuè Zàng. That it was refuted only after Master Zàng had passed away is likely because the Master [Mǐn] had only recently seen his books.
Is this not, in essence, a single grand falsehood regarding both mundane and supramundane paths? Just as he was about to...
The transmission of the Seven Patriarchs has been scrutinized with such meticulousness as to seek out every flaw, leaving no effort unexerted.
Yet, regarding the single work *Wuzongyuan*, which I have held in my hands for five or six years, it is said that I have only just now seen it—how could this be reasonable?

I have heard that Master Min was also a man of integrity and, moreover, trained under the mallet and whisk of his late teacher at Tiantong; that teacher was renowned for his straightforward mind and straightforward conduct.
If he had summoned the monastics throughout the realm, it would certainly not have been his own doing.
That being the case, whether it be a book or a preface, how could it be anything other than a forgery? Throughout my life, I have been extremely lazy about reading books;

as for the *Record of the An-yin* sent by Han Yue, I did not know how many years had passed until the evening of the twentieth day of the first month of the Gengchen year, when I finally ordered my attendant to fetch it.

"Furthermore, I have been looking through all the recorded sayings of the Han Moon (Han Yue) masters. When the Abbot [Tuo] unfolded several scrolls, I too laughed at his ignorance that such records existed.

Had it not been for the General Discourse by Dingmu and the critical remarks of Layman Liu, I certainly would not have sought out the *Wuzongyuan* (The Source of the Five Houses). Thus, it came about that Muchen had a teacher."
Recently, I have finally seen the preface to his writings; it is indeed a veritable record (*shilu*). If that is so, then are the writings themselves forged?
Why not ask the old monk [Tanhui] about this? Is the preface itself forged? Why not ask Muchen [Hongyun]? Furthermore, Tanji’s preface states: [Insert the remainder of the passage here]

yet the Elder [Buddha] still remains in all his dignity. Who, then, has composed these spurious texts? You further ask: "How could one dare to emulate the righteousness of Fusu? No.

I requested it once again. Consequently, there was an engraved copy of the *Wujia zhengzong jiu* (The Rescue of the Five Schools), which you have instead concealed and hidden, not allowing this old monk to see it even once.
What is the purpose of this? You falsely claim that my refutation is a forgery, hoping that people will set it aside and not look at it;
yet you carve the *Wujia zhengzong jiu* and distribute it widely to all others, while alone concealing this one old monk, so that for ten thousand generations...

Subsequently, those who were ignorant remarked: "During the lifetime of Tiantong, Tanji presented the *Wuzong jiu* (Rescue of the Five Schools) and further requested [instruction], yet we have never heard a single word from Tiantong correcting its errors. Thus, it is perfectly clear that the *Pishi* (Refutation) was a forgery."

This was merely you all deceiving your own hearts and obscuring yourselves, giving rise to such treacherous and cunning schemes to deceive the Buddhas and Patriarchs, to deceive the dragons and devas, and to deceive the world for ten thousand generations.

In the autumn of the Jǐmǎo year, this old monk, on account of the matter of repairing a stupa, took up his staff and crossed the river, briefly resting at Meixi Hermitage in Jiāxìng. Tíngmù broke open the stone, and Jùdé followed to succeed him.
The lay practitioners Huirun, Dengjie, Zhang'er, Wu, Wangjin, Ru, Qiji, and Chao came to request that I perform a rite of repentance,
wishing for the destruction of the printing blocks of the Five Houses and the removal of all verbose and entangling words from the *Yulu* (Recorded Sayings) of Han Yue.
Qiu Laoseng asked, "Why not refute the *Wuzong jiu*? The old monk laughed and said, "Whether or not to destroy the woodblocks is a matter for your descendants.
Since the *Wuzong jiu* has already been carved and circulated, it must be refuted; this is a matter for me, the old monk. Why is this?
It is just as when Kongyin’s *Zhengliang lun* refuted the 'Non-transmigration of Things. I, Long..."
The Elder Chi had previously offered critical remarks [regarding the *Nyāyānusāra*]. When Kongyin was approaching his death, he instructed more than ten attendant monks, saying:
"After my passing, you may burn the woodblocks for the *Sāmmitīya-nikāya-śāstra*. Do not allow me to incur further offense against the ancients. He then composed a verse, which said:
"My profound treatises throughout my life were praised as preeminent by all; yet when it comes to the moment of death, my skillful means..."
It is exhausted. The bucket has never lost its bottom; yet you speak at random of the five aggregates being originally empty. The board has already been split.
Recently, there have been those who have carved it out anew, such as Daoheng. Now that the *Rescue of the Five Schools* has already been carved and circulated.
Even if they were to destroy those wooden blocks, who in the world or in future generations would know that there might be those who fall victim to their poison?
Had the Old Monk not stepped forward to rescue and correct them, Han Yue, Tanji, and the others would have remained in hell forever, with no day of emergence in sight.
At that time, Dingmu returned home first under the pretext of illness and had not yet heard this account. When Juede heard of it, he did not take leave but departed in secret.
[He] fled. The others each withdrew with humble acquiescence.
[Someone] rescued [the letter], saying: "This was a handwritten letter sent by the Elder Master Tiandong while the Former Teacher was dwelling in peace and security.
This letter dates from the first year of the Chongzhen era. The 'Seven Refutations' and 'Three Refutations' appeared in the seventh year. Nine.
How many years have passed? Yet, amidst the myriad forms of insults and derision, have you perhaps completely forgotten these words?
Alas! This book states that during the private interrogations within the room, there was no trace of conceptual understanding;
yet this [other] book treats them as belonging to the school of conceptual understanding. This book states that throughout the several scrolls of public sermons, every word was precise and lucid.

[He] was truly worthy of succession. Yet, the "Refutation" (Pìshū) treats him as a mere "spirit of the bamboo leaves"—one whose karmic consciousness is vast and wandering, with no fundamental basis to rely upon.
How could this possibly be the mind of the Buddhas and Patriarchs? Alas! This [work] clearly originated from the hand of our late teacher Tiantong;
as for the "Refutation," I know nothing of it. Or perhaps it is merely the work of one who looks on at affairs with a penchant for controversy.
"Did people instigate him to do this? Mencius said, "In ancient times, people cultivated their heavenly rank (*tianjue*), and the human rank (*renjue*) followed of its own accord.
In the present day, people cultivate their heavenly rank merely to solicit the human rank; once they have obtained the human rank, they immediately cast aside their heavenly rank.
In the end, they will surely perish. As for my old monk’s observation of Tan Ji’s attempt to save [himself], it is precisely..."
The principles of Heaven are manifest. Why is this a case where the culprit confesses without being struck?
This letter of mine was written in the first year of the Chongzhen era; Han Yue’s *Wuzongyuan* appeared in the spring of the third year. I, the old monk, said:

"The single word 'original' (yuan) does not appear in the Way of the Sixth Patriarch; it is a term of those who follow the school of intellectual understanding, and thus I could not help but expose it."
This old monk’s single-minded compassion is solely for the sake of ensuring that Han Yue prospers.

In the summer of the sixth year, he again wrote to Han Yue, saying: "The dilapidated hall is leaking from the rain, and the thatched path remains uncleared; this is the common lot of those who dwell on a mountain.
I especially wish that my disciples, for the sake of the community, shall always maintain a straightforward mind and intention, remaining true to the authentic essence."
"Portion. It is not permissible to privately apply a separate dharma to the assembly; this is what this old monk hopes for. Furthermore, have you not seen the old monk’s compassionate heart?
I simply wish for Han Yue to be well. In the summer of the sixth year, he again cited the words of Muzhou, saying:
"In the *Record of Rui Guang*, there is a passage where he exalts the True Dharma on behalf of Ciyun; this seems to be a case of excessive forced interpretation."
I am an old monk, grown very old indeed; it is certainly not fitting for me to intervene in such discernment. Furthermore, my wisdom and insight are dim and short-sighted;
I do not see who is the guest and who is the host, nor how the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials could possibly exist within one's breast.
I would have no reason to weigh gain and loss with you, were it not because you claim to be my grandson. If I do not briefly...
If you bring this up, then bystanders and future generations will all say it was the old monk’s fault.
It was just like when the two head seats of the hall simultaneously shouted; the monk then asked Linji, "Is there still guest and host?"
Ji said: "The guest and the host are clearly distinct. Let me try asking my grandson:
since both of you shouted at the same time, try to discern which one is the guest and which one is the host.
If you can discern this, you may distinguish between host and guest and speak of guest and host. If you cannot discern it, do not speak or divide them haphazardly. When he had finished speaking—
At first, Hong Juefan had a point of insight regarding this, yet he mistakenly identified it as the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials;
for this reason, from antiquity to the present, he has not escaped the laughter of those with true discernment. However, there is a point where he errs:
he says, "Look closely, and this is the 'Tiger-Trapping' device. Suddenly, with a single thunderous boom, the "Poison-Coated Drum" sounds. Do you not see Master Fuguo? He requested—
He asked Master Wuzu Yan, “How are the guest and host in Linji’s teaching? Wuzu said, “That too is merely a matter of formal procedure; what idle business is it?
Here in my place, it is just like wrestling in front of a horse: as soon as one is thrown down, it is over.
The old monk thought back to when Master Fenyang Shao was alive; even then, there were already those like you who falsely clung to the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials. Therefore—
I have composed this verse as a warning: The Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials are difficult to distinguish; When one attains the meaning and forgets the words, the Way is easy to approach.
A single phrase clearly encompasses the myriad phenomena; On the Double Ninth, the chrysanthemums are fresh. Since it is said that one "forgets words," how could it be as you imagine?
From antiquity to the present, those who have personally realized the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials have each pointed them out one by one.
A person who has received the seal of approval from a master may be said to have reached a depth beyond depth and a mystery beyond mystery.
Yet when I, this old monk, ask you, "How thick is your face?"—it is because the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials originate from Linji’s formal discourse, which states:
"Every single word must embody the three mysteries; every mystery must embody the three essentials; there must be both the provisional and the real."
"Use it! How do you all understand this? The old monk said as he descended from his seat, "How do you all understand this?
It is simply that you, my disciples, have not yet seen even a dream of it. If you can see it, then examine it for me:
where is the place where he possesses power? Where is the place where he has utility? At that time...
Ciming once responded to a monk’s request for instruction on the Three Mysteries and the One Essential Point. Although he provided a verse for each one, he concluded by summarizing them all:
"I tell you, you seeker of the profound mystery: the staff and the shout must be applied according to the occasion. If you clearly understand the direct intent, the great sun shines even at midnight.
Since Ciming had thus brought them back into a single unity, how could there ever have been even a shadow of the Three Mysteries and the One Essential Point left behind?
"I have lured you here. Let the old monk question you once more: Since you have attained self-awakening, why are there the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials?
If you have already awakened to the Three Mysteries and the Three Essentials, how can this be called 'self-awakening'? Is this not a contradiction of your own words?"
Your own words are self-contradictory. Furthermore, you claim to be upholding the True Dharma; why do you not look at what Linji said?

"Who would have known that my Treasury of the True Dharma Eye would perish upon the blind donkey? He also said: "If one asks how it is when the current flows on without ceasing, tell him it is boundless true illumination.
One who is free from marks and names does not receive [the transmission]; it is like using a 'blow-off' sword."

One must realize that this requires immediate polishing; how could it be like your insistence on fixed names and characteristics regarding the Three Mysteries and Three Essentials as a means of exalting the True Dharma?
To dare claim to be a descendant of Linji—my grandson, please reflect deeply upon this.
